abstract: Let $n=2m\ge 4$ and $d\ge 2$ be even, let $I=\{0,m\}\subset\mathbb{Z}_n$, and let $H_{d,n}$ be the Latin hypercube obtained from the cyclic hypercube $(x_1,\dots,x_d)\mapsto x_1+\dots+x_d$ by adding $m$ to the symbol of every cell of $I^d$, that is, by turning one subhypercube of order $2$. Child and Wanless (arXiv:2605.01813) introduced $H_{d,n}$ as a Latin hypercube of even order and dimension that has transversals although the cyclic hypercube has none; every transversal of $H_{d,n}$ meets $I^d$, so $H_{d,n}$ has at most $2^d$ disjoint transversals. Based on computations for small parameters, they conjectured that every entry of $H_{d,n}$ lies in a transversal. We prove this conjecture for all even $d\ge 2$ and all even $n\ge 4$. For $d=2$ we construct explicit two-parameter families of transversals from a bijection between punctured integer intervals whose sums are consecutive odd integers, and show that their images under the twelve coordinate-symbol symmetries and the translations by $I^2$ cover all $n^2$ cells. For $d\ge 4$ we argue by induction on $d$ in steps of two. If two entries of the graph tuple of the target cell sum into $I$, a transversal of $H_{d-2,n}$ lifts directly; otherwise transversals of $H_{d-2,n}$ and $H_{2,n}$ are glued along a two-dimensional transversal of symbol pairs, using two coverage properties of normalized two-dimensional transversals that we prove for every even $n$. A Python implementation of the construction and an independent checker verify one transversal through each of the $328{,}760$ cells for the $11$ pairs $(n,d)$ with $n\le 10$, $d\le 6$ and $n^d\le 8^6$, and the explicit formulas of Sections 2 and 3 are checked over finite ranges up to $n=100$; these finite checks support but do not replace the proof. The result concerns this one family and gives no information on the number of transversals or on decompositions into transversals.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
- Added a motivating paragraph at the start of Section 3.4 (before Propositions 3.6 and 3.7) explaining in ordinary language how paired-triple coverage supplies the two degrees of freedom needed to choose compatible special symbols in Case 3 of Theorem 4.4 (shifting the required normalized triples by (0,m,m) and (m,m,0)), and clarified that Proposition 3.6 (when s_1 in I) and Proposition 3.7 (when s_1 not in I) handle the first coverage problem whereas Proposition 3.7 handles the second coverage problem regardless of whether s_1 in I.
- Added a schematic summary table after Lemma 4.3 contrasting the n-1 ordinary symbol pairs (s_1,s_2) != (a_0,b_0) in T_g with the unique special symbol pair (a_0,b_0) in T_g cap I_2, illustrating how the turn corrections on T_1 in H_{d-2,n} and T_2 in H_{2,n} combine into the single +m turn correction on I_d.
- Replaced the empirical observation after Table 1 in Section 5 with the two-part structural proof showing why Case 3 never occurs when n = 4 in any even dimension d >= 4 and why Case 3.2 (s_1 in I) never occurs when d = 4 for any even n >= 4, enforced in build.py.
- Wrote out explicit intermediate domain/image and residue steps in Lemma 2.3(iv), Proposition 3.7 (B.1, B.2, B.2.2(ii)), and Theorem 4.4 (Case 3), and updated the author line to the standard affiliation format.
- Expanded Section 1.1 with exact theorem, display, and table locators into Child-Wanless [1], Wanless [2], Egan-Wanless [3], Ghafari-Wanless [4], and Luria [5], and corrected the two literature descriptions identified in the review of submission -uhOvUI6RkG93M5g: (i) noted that H_{d,n} (n = 2m) is the m-dilation [1, Section 4, p. 10] of the order-2 Latin hypercube K(u_1,...,u_d) = u_1 + ... + u_d + 1 (mod 2), while explaining why the dilation lemmas [1, Lemmas 17-18] (which require d odd or m odd and relate (Z_n,d)-suitable diagonals through I_d to those of K) do not establish entry coverage of H_{d,n}; and (ii) stated accurately that for every even n >= 10, Ghafari-Wanless [4, Theorems 1.1, 1.2, and 2.2] constructed a Latin square of order n with a transversal, at least floor(n/6) entries shared by every (Z_n,2)-suitable diagonal (and every transversal, quoted in [1, Theorem 11]), and tau(L) >= 19n^2/36 + O(n) transversal-free entries (as well as order n = 3m squares for odd m >= 3 in [4, Theorem 1.3]).
- Retained identical supplementary scripts and all 11 witness SHA-256 digests from v1, with the summary record, generation log, and SHA-256 digest list in the supplement refreshed by the deterministic rebuild.
title: Every entry of the turned cyclic Latin hypercube lies in a transversal
